newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes attack south south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes attack south south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli planes rocketed suspected Hizbollah guerrilla targets in south Lebanon on Sunday, security sources said.
They said two Israeli planes fired two rockets into the hills of Jabal Safi and Mleeta in the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge -- a bastion of the Moslem guerrillas.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air attack -- the 37th into Lebanon since the beginning of the year.

Earlier on Sunday, pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas attacked an Israeli outpost inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone with machinguns and rocket-propelled grenades, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
There were no casualties in the attack on the Sojoud outpost, they added.
Shortly before the air raid, residents of a south Lebanon village said Israeli forces advanced into their area and arrested six Lebanese civilians.

They said an Israeli motorised patrol advanced one km (0.5 mile) outside the zone into the village of Arnoun, established a temporary checkpoint and arrested six Lebanese men before pulling back into the occupied area.
The operation lasted less than two hours, residents who arrived in the nearby village of Kfar Tibnit in south Lebanon's central sector told reporters.
Israel occupies a 15-km (nine-mile) -wide zone in south Lebanon and Moslem guerrillas attack Israeli and allied forces in a bid to oust them from the area.
